situation.summary: Tenant Nia Calder reported on 4 Aug 2025 a constantly dripping kitchen mixer tap with cloudy-looking water, and asked whether a new tap could be considered. The landlord approved "maintenance works" on 5 Aug (E003), but no price or replacement was approved. Scheduling with the contractor, Ivo Fenlock, dragged for five weeks. A visit for 10 Sep was confirmed late, and no record shows whether it happened. On 15 Sep the contractor sent an invoice, later corrected for postcode, for a new mono kitchen sink tap supplied and installed. The invoice amount is not in the readable copy, and no record shows the visit outcome, a repair-versus-replace decision, or landlord approval of a replacement. The tenant has had no reply from us since 9 Sep, and her drawer question (E012) is unanswered.
situation.task: Verify the 10 Sep visit and the replacement-tap invoice with the contractor, and tell the landlord and tenant where things stand, before anyone approves the invoice.
situation.stageLabel: Corrected invoice received for a replacement mono kitchen tap; visit outcome and landlord approval of that scope not verified
situation.whoseMove: Our move (Tessa Wren, Northbridge). Send the contractor an email today asking to confirm the 10 Sep visit outcome, the work done, why a new tap was fitted, and the invoice amount and VAT basis, with a reply by Wed 17 Sep 2025. In the same turn send the landlord a short update that a replacement tap has been invoiced and is not treated as approved, and tell the tenant what is being checked and when she will hear (by Wed 17 Sep 2025). After that the landlord must decide on scope and price, and the tenant must confirm whether the drip has stopped.

decision.actionLabel: Ask Bracken & Vale Plumbing for the invoice amount and VAT, a completion report and photos for the new kitchen tap, and confirmation that the spare key was returned, before the invoice goes to the landlord
decision.message:
Hi Ivo,

Thank you for the corrected invoice (ref NBL-025-INV-15) for 18 Thistlewick Row, Fenmere, ZZ1 1ZZ, which now shows the right postcode.

Before I can pass it to the landlord, I need the following, please:

1. A readable PDF of the invoice showing the amount, the VAT basis (VAT-registered or not, and the VAT figure if it applies) and the line items. The copy we have shows the work but no amount.
2. The date you attended and a short completion note. Please tell us whether the old mixer tap could have been repaired, and why you fitted a new mono tap instead. The landlord approved maintenance on the dripping tap. He did not approve a particular replacement or price.
3. Before and after photos of the tap.
4. Did you notice or check anything about the tenant's report of cloudy-looking water when filling a glass? If so, please tell us what you found.
5. Confirmation that you collected the agency's spare key and returned it to our office, and the date you returned it.

Please reply by Wednesday 17 September 2025. Please do not carry out any further work at the property until we confirm the landlord's approval.

The boiler matter you raised on today's call is separate, and I'll pick it up with the relevant engineer apart from this job.

Kind regards,
Tessa Wren
Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings
decision.rationale: The stage is "evidence before forwarding the invoice". A corrected invoice for a new mono kitchen tap has arrived (E022, A1), but the readable copy shows no amount or VAT basis. We cannot check it against an approval or forward it as it stands. The only sign the work was done is the contractor's own invoice. Nothing records whether the 10 Sep visit happened (E016–E018), and there are no photos or completion notes. The landlord approved "maintenance works" (E003), and we had asked the contractor for a quote or advice (E004). A full replacement tap needs explaining before it goes to the landlord, so the contractor holds every missing fact. The agency spare key was authorised for the visit (E015), and the office needs to know it has come back. In the same turn, the tenant is asked to confirm the fix. She has heard nothing from us since 12 Aug (E009), and her drawer report (E012) is unanswered. The landlord gets a status update and is asked about the drawer, without being told the work is complete.
decision.expectedOutcome: The contractor sends an invoice PDF with the amount and VAT, the visit date, the reason for replacing the tap, photos, and confirmation that the key was returned. The tenant confirms whether the drip has stopped. We can then send the invoice to the landlord with the evidence, flagging the replacement against his approval.
boundaries: An invoice is not evidence of completion until the tenant or a completion report confirms it.
This does not approve or pay the invoice. The landlord has approved maintenance, not a specific replacement or price.
This does not diagnose the cloudy water or say it is safe.
The drawer repair is not authorised; it needs the landlord's decision.
The boiler matter is not part of this job and is not settled here.
remainingWork: Once the amount is known, compare it with the landlord's approval and send the invoice to the landlord with the evidence, flagging that the tap was replaced rather than repaired.
Get the landlord's decision on the drawer, then assign if he approves.
Check the office key log to confirm the spare key is back.
Check the boiler matter with the relevant engineer, separately from this job.
Close the job once the fix is confirmed, the landlord has the invoice, the payment route is noted and the key is back.
assumptions: The visit probably happened between 10 and 15 Sep, given the invoice, but this is not confirmed.
The landlord is back from abroad and email is still the best route (E003).

alternatives.whyNot: There is no amount or VAT on the readable copy, no completion evidence, and the tap was replaced when the approval covered maintenance. Forwarding now would present unverified work and cost.

decision.rationale: The visit was approved (E003). The contractor has now invoiced a new mono tap, and a corrected copy is on file (E019, E022). But the only readable copy (A1) has no amount and no VAT basis. Nothing records the visit date, why the tap was replaced rather than repaired, any photos, or the return of the agency spare key (E015, E016, E018). We had asked for a quote or advice first (E004), and the tenant had raised a new tap as a question (E001), so the replacement needs explaining before the landlord sees it. The manual says not to forward an invoice we cannot check against the approval, and to ask the contractor for missing evidence. The only evidence of completion is the contractor's own invoice, so in the same turn we ask the tenant to confirm the fix. Her drawer report (E012) has gone unanswered, so we acknowledge it to her. We hold the landlord update until the amount and her confirmation are in, so we don't tell him the job is done without evidence.
decision.expectedOutcome: The contractor sends the full invoice PDF with the amount and VAT basis, the visit date, why the tap was replaced, photos and the key status. Asking for the amount does not approve or pay the invoice. Whether the landlord accepts a replacement tap he never priced is his decision.
Nothing here says what caused the cloudy water or whether it is safe. That stays with qualified people.
The drawer is a separate repair and has not been approved. Acknowledging it does not commit anyone to repair it.
The boiler matter raised on the call (E021) is separate and is not covered by this message.
remainingWork: Once the amount and the tenant's confirmation are in, update the landlord (Orin Bell, by email): what was done, the invoice and its amount, and that he is being asked to accept a replacement tap. If he does not accept the replacement or its cost, hand to a person.
Ask the landlord whether our contractor should look at the loose kitchen drawer with the snapped brackets (E012).
Check with the relevant engineer about the boiler matter raised on the call (E021). Keep it off this job.
Confirm the spare key is back in the office before closing.
If the contractor has not replied by 17 Sep, phone them.
assumptions: The corrected invoice copy we hold (A1) is the whole readable document and has no amount on it.
The contractor attended on or around 10 Sep using the office spare key. This is not recorded.

The invoice has not been checked or forwarded, the landlord has not been told, the fix is unconfirmed, the key's whereabouts are unknown, and the drawer question is open.

problems.issue: c1 [scope] The landlord note says "Nothing will be paid until you have seen it". The records don't show who pays or how, and this commits the agency to a payment route that nobody has confirmed. (E003, E022, A1). Fix: Drop that sentence, or say only that the invoice and evidence will come to him for review before anything is settled.

c2 [safety] The tenant message tells her to avoid putting weight on the drawer. That is informal repair or handling advice on a fault nobody has assessed. (E012). Fix: Remove it, or limit it to "tell us if it gets worse".

c3 [communication] The contractor email brings in the boiler matter from the call. That is a separate topic and isn't needed for this ask. The tenant message also says the contractor "has told us they have fitted" the tap, but the only source is an invoice with no completion note. (E021, E022, A1). Fix: Cut the boiler line from the contractor email. Word the tenant message as "we have received an invoice for a new tap".
